findings.reason: if the search had been run the author would have found the existing gate vocabulary and either extended it or justified a fork, which is the whole decision §25 turns on.
findings.text: the reuse map for §25's relevance decision already exists as CodeFile's `triage_*` dimension scores (`triage_data_access` 2992, `triage_imas` 3004, `triage_documentation` 3001, `triage_modeling_code` 2983) and its `score_*` siblings (`score_data_access` 2957, `score_imas` 2966), driven by the `discovery-triage` seat and `imas_codex/llm/prompts/code/triage.md`; the plan's design text cites the call layer, `render_prompt`, `get_model` and `facility.data_access_patterns` as reuse, but never this mechanism, so the reviewer cannot tell whether the author searched it

findings.reason: a parallel seat plus template for one function doubles the surface a future scope change would need to keep in step, and the honest change is to widen the existing prompt and its `discovery-triage` seat.
findings.text: §25 introduces `discovery-relevance` as a new seat and `code/relevance.md` as a new prompt for the triage stage, a second thin layer over the same `discovery-triage` seat and `code/triage.md` prompt that already occupy the triage call site (`imas_codex/discovery/code/scorer.py:256`), with no stated reason the existing seat and template cannot carry the widened L/P/G/I questions

findings.reason: naming the existing dimension owner lets the author widen its rubric for the new scope rule instead of forking a second vocabulary that the ingest gate and any downstream indicator count would then have to join across two field families.
findings.text: the eight proposed CodeFile fields duplicate the existing triage and scoring dimension family: `relevance_loads` duplicates `triage_data_access` (facility.yaml:2992), `relevance_imas` duplicates `triage_imas` (3004) and `score_imas` (2966), `relevance_describes` duplicates `triage_documentation` (3001) and `score_documentation` (3071), `relevance_simulation` duplicates `triage_modeling_code` (2983) and `score_modeling_code`, and `relevance_role` overlaps the DiscoveryRootCategory taxonomy the per-purpose scores are already aligned to; six of the eight fields restate an owner that already exists, and the plan leaves the old dimensions orphaned rather than migrating them

findings.reason: the section must account for the interface it adds in its own text as the rule requires, and doing so is what forces the retire/merge decision that also resolves the reuse and duplicate findings above.
findings.text: §25 adds surface by adding `call_decisions` and `acall_decisions` beside `call_llm_structured`, a new `discovery-relevance` seat, `code-triage-threshold` and `code-ingest-threshold` settings, and eight CodeFile fields, and the section text retires or merges nothing (it only narrows `--min-score`'s existing reading and names no surface it drops), nor says why nothing can be

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `call_decisions()`/`acall_decisions()`, placed beside `call_llm_structured` in the owning `imas_codex/discovery/base/llm.py`, hide the request shape, per-answer validation, retry and cost extraction behind one call; §14's `build_path_prefix_filter` (`imas_codex/graph/query_builder.py:282`) likewise bundles clause and bound parameters behind one call.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §25 adds eight `relevance_*` CodeFile fields beside an existing triage/scoring dimension family that already encodes the same concepts; the owner to extend is the CodeFile dimension set in `imas_codex/schemas/facility.yaml:2957-3006`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §25 adds two public functions (`call_decisions`, `acall_decisions`), a new `discovery-relevance` seat, two settings and eight schema fields, and names nothing it retires or merges, nor why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §25 reuses the call, prompt, seat and facility-pattern machinery, but never cites the pre-existing per-dimension code triage taxonomy (`triage_data_access`/`triage_imas`/`triage_documentation` at `imas_codex/schemas/facility.yaml:2983-3006`) or the `discovery-triage` seat and `code/triage.md` prompt that already do what the new relevance subsystem is about to add.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the new `discovery-relevance` seat and `imas_codex/llm/prompts/code/relevance.md` template are a parallel layer over the existing code triage mechanism (`discovery-triage` seat at `imas_codex/settings.py:144`, `code/triage.md`, `apply_triage_results` at `imas_codex/discovery/code/scorer.py:445`), and the design does not say why that mechanism cannot be extended to the widened scope rule instead.
